levels.label: Levels
levels.description: XP per message, levels, reward roles and leaderboard.

rang.description: Show your level, XP and rank.
rang.member: The member whose rank to show (default: you).
rang.noXp: This member hasn't earned any XP yet.
rang.title: {user}'s level

leaderboard.empty: Nobody has earned XP on this server yet.
leaderboard.title: 🏆 Leaderboard

g0.label: ⚙️ XP gain

xpMin.label: Minimum XP per message
xpMin.help: The floor of the roll. It sets the baseline pace: a regular member earns roughly the average of the two bounds per counted message.

xpMax.label: Maximum XP per message
xpMax.help: The ceiling of the roll. Setting it far above the minimum makes progress erratic and discouraging; setting it equal to the minimum removes the randomness.

cooldown.label: Cooldown between gains (s)
cooldown.help: During this delay, further messages from the same member earn nothing. This is the module's anti-spam guard: at 0, ten one-word messages pay ten times, and the leaderboard rewards noise instead of presence.

maxLevel.label: Maximum level (0 = unlimited)
maxLevel.help: Beyond it, XP keeps being counted but the level stops rising and no announcement is sent. Useful so veterans don't leave newcomers permanently behind. 0 lifts the cap.

ignoredChannelIds.label: Ignored channels
ignoredChannelIds.help: No gain is counted there, by message or in voice. Best kept for test channels, bot-command channels and spam channels — anywhere writing a lot means nothing.

ignoredRoleIds.label: Ignored roles
ignoredRoleIds.help: Members holding any of these roles stop earning anything, wherever they write. Mostly for secondary bots and service accounts; it is also the quietest sanction against someone inflating their counter.

boosterRoleIds.label: Roles with an XP bonus
boosterRoleIds.help: Members holding any of these roles have their gain multiplied. Roles do not stack: holding two does not double twice.

boosterMultiplier.label: Bonus multiplier
boosterMultiplier.help: How much XP is multiplied by for the roles above. Past 2, a boosted member catches up in a week what another took a month to earn, and the leaderboard stops showing who takes part.

voiceEnabled.label: XP in voice channels
voiceEnabled.help: Also counts time spent in voice channels. A member alone, deafened or muted earns nothing: otherwise leaving a tab open overnight would be enough.

voiceXpPerMinute.label: XP per minute in voice
voiceXpPerMinute.help: Paid for each minute spent in voice with company. Weigh it against the per-message gain: an hour of voice should not be worth a week of writing, nor the other way round.

leaderboardChannelId.label: Leaderboard channel
leaderboardChannelId.help: The bot keeps a single leaderboard message there, rewritten every ten minutes rather than reposted. Leave it empty for no standing leaderboard — the command still works.

g0.description: Every message earns a random amount between the minimum and the maximum. The randomness is there so nobody can work out the exact number of messages needed to level up — closing the gap between the two bounds makes progress mechanical.

g1.label: 🏅 Role rewards
g1.description: Role granted automatically when a member reaches the given level.

rewards.label: Roles by level
rewards.help: One row per tier. The bot must be able to grant these roles: they have to sit BELOW its own role in the server hierarchy, otherwise granting fails silently. A role already earned is never taken back.

announce.label: 📣 Level-up announcement

enabled.label: Enable the announcement
enabled.help: Off, levels are still counted and roles still granted — nothing announces it any more.

channelId.label: Channel (empty = the message's channel)
channelId.help: Empty, the announcement is posted in the channel the member just wrote in: it lands where they are looking. A fixed channel avoids interrupting conversations, at the cost of being seen less.

message.label: Message
message.help: Variables replaced when sent: {mention} to address the member, {level} for their new level. A misspelt variable is shown as written.

announce.description: One announcement per level-up, at the moment it happens. Never a batched catch-up.
